what_to_record_before_data_collection: Document hearing/hearing-screen policy, headphone or transducer check, listening-room/background-noise notes, level-setting procedure, and whether participant-ear SPL was measured or estimated.
current_toolkit_state: The runner records selected output route, output-level settings, audio checks, and loudness-policy metadata; the manuscript distinguishes estimated SPL from measured calibration.
required_before_strong_claim: A publication example that makes auditory or spatial-perception claims should attach the screening script/results, room or headphone policy, sound-level measurement or level-setting artifact, and any exclusion rule.
boundary: Route selection and successful audio playback are not evidence of normal hearing, headphone compliance, externalization, or participant-ear SPL.

what_to_record_before_data_collection: Record SOFA/HRTF resource, renderer/version, trajectory frame, headphones/transducers, level law, and any localization/externalization or front-back check.
current_toolkit_state: Renderer manifests preserve FABIAN/SOFA or 3DTI-compatible provenance, trajectory, channel map, source hashes, and loudness policy.
required_before_strong_claim: Strong claims about perceived distance, direction, externalization, or individualized HRTF validity need a participant-level spatial-perception check or an explicit limitation statement.
boundary: HRTF/SOFA provenance documents stimulus generation, not participant-level perceived space.

what_to_record_before_data_collection: Record operating system, app/runner version, audio interface, channel map, buffer/sample-rate settings, response device, LSL/LabRecorder state, loopback wiring, and reconciliation hashes.
current_toolkit_state: The runner writes software schedules, event logs, LSL marker mirrors, optional LabRecorder XDF, audio evidence WAVs, and optional electrical loopback files.
required_before_strong_claim: Publication-hardware timing claims need a route-specific validation archive with response-device checks, audio/tactile channel evidence, loopback method, reconciliation report, and tool versions.
boundary: Software markers and digital audio buffers do not by themselves prove physical sound, tactile onset, or response-device latency.

what_to_record_before_data_collection: Record tactile actuator, body site, threshold assay settings, accepted output value, confirmation counters, misses, top-up policy, adaptive-threshold settings, and any mechanical/electrical timing measurement.
current_toolkit_state: Focus Mode includes a participant-specific tactile threshold assay, miss logging, top-up, and a run-local two-miss adaptive nudge with CSV/JSON artifacts.
required_before_strong_claim: Strong tactile-delivery claims need calibration examples plus mechanical/electrical or perceptual evidence appropriate to the actuator and body site.
boundary: The adaptive nudge and top-up are operator safeguards; they do not prove habituation correction, mechanical onset, or perceived tactile delivery.

what_to_record_before_data_collection: Record baseline strategy, catch trials, repetitions, block order, response window, exclusion rules, planned cell counts, and whether instant-analysis outputs are exploratory or confirmatory.
current_toolkit_state: Segments 3-6 materialize baseline/catch files, repetition pools, block CSVs, participant schedules, response rules, and analysis artifacts with hashes.
required_before_strong_claim: Confirmatory claims need a preregistered analysis plan, adequate cell counts, response-probability reporting, and baseline-correction decisions fixed before inspection.
boundary: A balanced schedule or attractive curve does not rule out expectancy, response-probability, or flexible-analysis confounds.

what_to_record_before_data_collection: Record source-paper status, missing parameters, substitutions, stimulus rights, profile hashes, generated assets, and which profile claims are exact, partial, scaffolded, or local examples.
current_toolkit_state: Profile ledgers record verification state, represented fields, missing fields, rights/substitution notes, and Segment 0-6 materialization status.
required_before_strong_claim: Exact-recreation language requires source-paper/supplement review, rights clearance, apparatus notes, final profile hash, and validation evidence for the release state.
boundary: A runnable profile can still be a scaffold if original apparatus, stimuli, instructions, or analysis choices are missing.
